entries.en: Axis and Allied teams battle for control of strategic locations on the map.
Capture the strategic control points around the map to keep the balance of power in your favor.
A blinking indicator at the top of your HUD indicates that the location is not ready to be captured.
The flag will rise faster with more teammates around the capture point.
If your team captures all the locations on the map, you will win the War. If neither team captures all locations before the timer expires, the team who held the most locations the longest will win.
The team with the higher score wins the game. Killing the enemy is just one way to score. Medics can score big by reviving teammates; Support classes can distribute ammo.
Score the most points in order to win the match.
Coordinate with your team to defeat the enemy!
Return the flag in order to win the game.
As the flag carrier, you are able to throw down the flag if desired. This will allow you to use your current weapon.
The flag can be used as a melee weapon when you are the flag carrier.
As the flag carrier, you will not be able to operate a vehicle. Call up a teammate for a ride back.
If the flag icon at your home base is grayed out, your flag is missing. You will need to retrieve it before you can score.
Grab the neutral flag and take it to the opposing team base to win.
Capture and then defend the headquarters.
Be the first team to establish a headquarters, then defend it from the other team.
Once your team has set up an HQ, defend it from the other team to earn points.
Every time you die while defending your HQ adds extra time before you are able to respawn.
Shutting down an enemy's HQ will earn your team a small amount of points and reset the HQ locations.
Medics receive points for reviving teammates.
Riflemen get a devastatingly effective grenade launcher attachment.
The Assault class can lay down anti-personnel mines. Use them to defend strategic choke points and flags.
Support soldiers can resupply teammates with ammunition.
There are severe penalties for killing your teammates, including demotions.
Picking up dropped weapons is a good way to resupply your ammo.
The Bazooka and Panzershreck are most effective when you are prone and using ADS.
Use your melee attack to finish off the enemy at close range.
When using the B.A.R., shoot in short bursts to maintain your accuracy.
Killing your teammates will result in a severe point penalty.
Be constantly on the move to reduce your chances of being sniped by a Scout.
Look for buildings that provide cover when caught in an artillery strike.
You can still use your weapons when riding in the passenger seat of the truck or motorcycle.
Tanks are weak in the back - use the hatch gun to protect yourself.
The M1 Garand cannot be reloaded until the entire clip is spent.
Use smoke grenades to make it harder for the enemies to see you when attacking strategic points.
Look for MG34 mounting points on sandbags, low walls, and open windowsills.
ADS is an abbrievation for 'Aim Down Sight'. All weapons are more accurate when aiming down the sight.
Anti-personnel mines can be detonated by vehicles with minimal damage.
There are three types of grenades in the game: frag grenades, sticky grenades, and smoke grenades. Check your kit layout for which type you have.
Each class has its own kit layout. Pick the kit that matches your play style.
Chevrons above players show what rank they are, as well as point out your teammates.
Health regenerates over time. When injured, find a safe spot to recover.
You can earn points toward rank promotions by capturing flags or objectives, using class abilities and killing the other team.
You can cook off most grenades. Time the release carefully to induce maximum damage.
Keep your ears open for the sounds of a bouncing grenade.
Look for the gold star on the compass for the location of the current objective.
Sticky grenades can attach to any surface, including vehicles and people.
When revived by a Medic, you regain all of your health.
Watch the class ability icon to know when your ability is charged and ready for use.
If you have a grenade, you can mantle and destroy slow moving tanks occupied by the enemy.
Be careful when crossing open spaces on maps with vehicles to avoid being run over.
The tighter your weapon's crosshairs, the more accurate your shots.
Sprint to increase your run speed briefly, but watch your Stamina meter carefully.
Watch the Death Cam to find where that fatal shot came from.
Teammates can be easily identified by the rank chevrons over their heads.
The Axis are equipped with a P.38 type pistol. The Allies have a Colt .45 as a sidearm.
Review the Scoreboard to check team scores during a session.
If you can see the grenade icon, you are in the blast radius! Get out of there!
While Aiming Down Sight, you will move slower and will not be able to sprint.
If you get separated from your squad, locate them using the green markers on your compass.
Ammo packs cannot be picked up when you are already full on ammo.
The MG34 and the .30 cal have the largest clips of all the weapons, but these guns are very inaccurate when you are moving.
When standing, your movements have a greater affect on your accuracy. Going prone and holding your breath will give you the best accuracy.
Place anti-personnel mines at strategic chokepoints for maximum effect.
Soldiers are invulnerable after spawning, briefly, to prevent spawn camping.
You will not receive any damage by going prone and crawling through mines planted by other players.
If all the main paths are covered by Scouts, look around for an underground path.
Higher points on the battlefield can give scouts a wider angle on all the action.
Anti-personnel mines planted by teammates will be marked on the battlefield so that they can be easily avoided.
There are four different controller configurations. Choose the one that best fits your play style.
Anti-Armor Support can re-supply teammates, along with the ability to stop vehicles in their tracks.
Aim for a tank's undercarriage; it is the weakest part of the armor.
Rushing a player can be an advantage; you throw their aim off and can finish with a melee strike.
Aim for your enemies head when firing. A head shot drops enemies more quickly than shots to the legs or body.
Anti-personnel mines can be used to defend strategic map points. Be aware, they may only be set in dirt, grass, or other soft surfaces.
You can vote for your favorite map during the After Action Review if map voting is turned on.
Sprint before a jump to clear distances not normally possible.
A small bullseye icon will show up on the compass where a team Scout has called an artillery strike.
When an enemy fires his weapon, a small red icon appears on the compass at his current location.
All Allied soldiers carry the Colt .45 as a backup sidearm. Use it to finish off enemy soldiers or when running low on ammunition.
The MK II A-1 is the standard issue grenade for Allied soldiers. Use it to take out Axis soldiers hiding behind cover.
The Stielhandgranate or stick hand grenade is the standard issue grenade for Axis soldiers. Use it to take out Allied soldiers hiding behind cover.
Don't forget to bring a friend or two when driving a jeep. Jeeps can hold a gunner and a passenger in addition to a driver.
The Kar98 is carried by Axis riflemen. It is best used at medium or long range.
Light assault soldiers carry submachine guns, sticky grenades, and anti-personnel mines. They move faster than any other soldier.
Jumping while sprinting will drain your fatigue meter quickly.
The scoped Kar98 is carried by Axis scouts. It is best used at extremely long range.
The M1 Garand is carried by Allied riflemen. It is semi-automatic allowing for rapid fire and is best used from medium to long range.
Nothing matches the speed of a motorcycle. Hop into a motorcycle and race to an objective or leave your enemies in the dust.
The MP40 is carried by Axis light assault soldiers. It is best used in close quarters and its light weight allows for fast movement.
Axis heavy assault soldiers carry the MP44. Use it at short or medium range.
All Axis soldiers carry the P38 as a sidearm. Switch to it to finish off badly injured foes or when low on ammunition.
Axis Anti-Armor Support carry this anti-tank weapon. It is very effective against vehicles and ineffective against personnel.
Allied scouts carry the scoped Springfield sniper rifle. Find a hidden vantage point and use ADS to shoot enemies from long distances.
These slow moving behemoths come equipped with a 75mm general purpose gun and a .50 caliber coaxial machine gun.
Allied light assault soldiers carry the Thompson submachine gun. It is best used in close combat.
Be sure to use a trench gun at close range. Trench guns are highly inaccurate at longer distances.
Be on the lookout for jeeps, motorcycles, and tanks. Battles can be won or lost due to their extra firepower and mobility.
Every kit has strengths and weaknesses. Pay careful attention to their load out and weapon ratings to choose the kit best suited for you.
Listen carefully to the sounds around you. They provide many clues to what's happening during a battle.
Watch for bullet tracers flying through the air. They can reveal the location of a hidden Scout or Support gunner.
If you see the gun is about to overheat, stop or pace your rate of fire to let it cool down.
Use the kit selection menu to try out the different kits and find the one that best suits you.
A medic can revive teammates to full health when they are critically wounded. Look for soldiers with the white cross icon over their heads.

The brainchild of John Garand, the M1 was powerful, accurate and reliable. Chambered for the venerable .30-06 cartridge, the M1 was the first semi-automatic rifle in military use.
Attaching to the bayonet lug and extending over the barrel, the M7 grenade launcher enables the firing of a 3.5" finned, shaped-charge grenade from the M1 Garand.
This accurate and powerful bolt action rifle has an effective range of 600 yards. Due to its scope placement over the receiver, cartridges must be loaded individually .
The mainstay of the British Army during WWII, this 10-round bolt action rifle is rugged, accurate and reliable.
Caliber .303 bolt action rifle with scope
Dedicated sniper rifle based on the standard bolt action rifle. Range is effective to 800 yards.
The Browning Automatic Rifle was a robust, full automatic, gas-operated light squad machine gun with a detachable 20 round box magazine.
Powerful .12 gauge pump shot gun with six round capacity first issued to U.S. troops in World War One for trench assault and clearing. Brutal at close range.
Based on the Czech ZB vz.26 light machine gun. Employs a top-feeding 30 round curved magazine. 450 rounds per minute with a range of 300 yards.
The "Tommy Gun" was blow-back operated with a cyclic rate of 700 rounds per minute. Wartime M1A1 were fed by 20 or 30 round stick magazines and generally issued to officers and NCOs.
A quick and cheap weapon to arm British troops after Dunkirk. The Sten used a horizontally-mounted 32 round magazine chambered for 9mm, so captured German ammunition could be used.
Reliable belt fed, air-cooled recoil operated squad machine gun employed by U.S. troops during WWII. Cyclic rate of 400-600 rounds per minute with an effective range of 1000 yards.
The Browning M2 is an air cooled, belt-fed, recoil operated heavy machine gun designed after WWI and used on vehicles and aircraft. 550 RPM, effective range: 2200 yards.
Originally designed for aircraft, the Vickers K was mounted in pairs by British SAS to their jeeps for hit-and-run-tactics during WWII. Distinctive 60/100 round drum magazine.
Rocket-powered, recoilless anti-tank weapon employing a 3.5 pound High Explosive Anti-Tank (HEAT) round from a tube. It was inaccurate and best employed at ranges under 120 yards.
Hand grenade often referred to as a "pineapple" because of its cross-hatched exterior. Pulling the pin and releasing the spoon allows some time to "cook" the grenade before it explodes.
Easily transportable anti-personnel area denial munition. Once placed in the ground and covered, these mines will explode when pressure is applied to the detonator. Lethal blast radius of 30 meters.
Single action, semi automatic pistol adopted by the U.S. military prior to WWI. Powerful and rugged, the M1911 holds seven rounds in its magazine. Effective range of 50 feet.
The standard medium field howitzer used by U.S. forces in WWII. Fires high explosive 105mm ammunition. Range of 11,500 yards.
The standard German bolt-action rifle of WWII. Powerful and accurate, but slow firing. Five round internal magazine fed by stripper clips. Effective range of 500 yards.
The four-power sniper scope extends the accuracy of the Kar 98k, but blocks use of a stripper clip - a five round magazine must be loaded a round at a time. Effective range of 1000 yards.
7.92mm bolt action rifle with grenade launcher
Essentially a Kar98k employing a Schiessbecher or "firing cup" which fits over the end of the muzzle and fires a 30mm rifle grenade with the aid of a special cartridge.
The first successful semi-automatic rifle adopted by the German army in WWII. Based on captured Russian Tokarev SVT40 rifles. Reloads quickly from a 10-round detachable box magazine.
World's first assault rifle employing a shortened version of the German 7.92mm rifle cartridge in a 30 round detachable magazine. 500 rounds per minute. 300 meter range.
Automatic rifle developed for German paratroopers after the invasion of Crete. 20 round side mounted detachable box magazine. 900 rounds cyclic rate. 500 meter effective range.
Infamous submachine gun developed and used extensively by the German military during WWII. 32 round detachable stick magazine. 500 rounds per minute. 100 meter effective range.
Adopted for squad support roles by the German army in 1934. 7.92mm rifle cartridge belt or drum fed. 900 rounds per minute. Effective range of 1000 meters.
Made from stamped steel and famous for its distinctive 1200 round per minute rate of fire, the MG42 was designed as a replacement for the MG34. Belt fed and recoil operated.
Reusable anti-tank rocket launcher based on captured U.S. Bazookas. It employs an 88mm anti-tank rocket that can penetrate 200mm of armor. Effective range of 180 meters.
Six-barreled rocket-launching artillery piece often referred to as "Screaming Mimis" by the allied soldiers it bombarded. It fires six 75 lb 150mm rockets in ten seconds to a range of 4 miles.
Dreaded German anti-aircraft cannon developed in the 1930s and used infamously in anti-tank and artillery roles. 88mm high explosive, anti-tank rounds able to defeat 150mm armor at 2 kilometers.
Devastating four-barreled 20mm anti-aircraft cannon employed by German military in multiple roles. 220-480 rounds per minute rate of fire. Effective range of 2200 meters.
Heavy mortar developed by German army prior to WWII. Indirect artillery firing a 3.5kg 81mm round over 2 kilometers. Effective blast radius of 50 meters.
Standard hand grenade used by German military throughout WWII. Referred to as "Potato Masher" by G.I.s because of its distinctive shape.
Sidearm issued to German military in WWII. Safer, more reliable and easier to manufacture than the Luger it replaced. 8 round magazine. Effective range of 25 meters.
4x4 general purpose transport and reconnaissance vehicle built by Willys-Overland and Ford Motor Co. Over 600,000 built.
A Willy's Jeep modified by the British SAS with up to 6 Vickers K fast-firing MGs for assault and defense. Used in long-range patrols and airdropped for operations in German-occupied France.
A workhorse transport with 6x6 off road capability, the "deuce-and-a-half" hauled troops, supplies and towed heavy loads in every theater of the war. Over 550,000 were produced.
Light tank used for infantry support. Steel beams cut from German beach obstacles and welded to the front enabled it to muscle through Normandy hedgerows.
Boxy armored troop transport based on the M4 Sherman tank. Essentially an M5 "Priest" self propelled artillery vehicle but without the 105mm gun.
The M4 was the standard U.S. medium tank. Although inferior in armament and armor to German medium and heavy tanks of the day, it was reliable and easy to manufacture.
